# CDB parser fixtures

`scoped.cdb` is synthetic, based on SPEC.md §3.4 and the SDCC team's
[CDB File Format](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/wiki/CDB%20File%20Format/).
It is not compiler-generated output and predates the adoption of the external
msxciv build as a fixture source. It includes links before declarations, an M record after declarations,
full Z80-style sublevels, register-plus-stack tails and a self-referencing type.

T support is intentionally limited to a single physical line containing
`Fmodule$tag[({offset}S:S$name$level$block({size}chain:sign),tail)...]`.
The tests demonstrate scalar members, pointer references, arrays and empty
member lists. The parser preserves encoded members; it does not infer sizes,
struct versus union, resolve reference graphs or certify a usable memory layout.
Bitfield members and unknown member type tokens are unsupported. Unsupported or
truncated T encodings produce localized diagnostics. F/S type chains remain
opaque (including unknown tokens) for the loader to resolve or reject.

Links remain separate from F/S declarations for cross-file reconciliation in the
loader. An X marker retains its inclusive address; no missing function entry,
exit, parameter classification or absolute variable address is synthesized.

`msxciv_sdcc_4_6_types.cdb` is a verbatim, minimal extract from
`projects/msxciv/out/msxciv.cdb`, generated by the bundled SDCC 4.6.0 with
`-mz80 --debug`. The source artifact contained 63,826 records, including 1,063
`T:` records. The extract deliberately preserves real encodings that the
synthetic fixture did not demonstrate: decimal array suffixes (`DA11d`), a
two-dimensional array, nested structs, a pointer to struct, a function pointer,
and bitfields (`SB...`). The fixture records both accepted encodings and the
current localized rejections, so phase 8 can promote each construction only
after its layout is demonstrated.

`phase8_types.c` is a dedicated evidence source compiled with the same bundled
SDCC 4.6.0 and Z80/debug flags used by msxciv. `phase8_types.adb` is the
compiler-generated debug fragment. `phase8_float_abi.json` records bytes copied
from the generated initializer assembly: `0.0f`, `1.0f`, and `-2.5f` match
IEEE-754 binary32 in little-endian order for this compiler/target combination.
